content.text: In C++, implement a checkout-price calculator for one caller-supplied item price. The item price, discount rate, and tax rate are exact decimal strings in plain nonnegative decimal notation: digits with an optional decimal point, and no sign, exponent, whitespace, or separator. Discount and tax rates must be in the inclusive range [0, 1] and are decimal fractions, so "0.1" means 10%. Return the final total as an exact decimal string with exactly two decimal places, rounded using half-even rounding. The caller selects standard or expedited shipping. Apply the discount only to the item price. If expedited shipping is used, add a 15.00 fee after that discount and before tax.

item.text: I’ll inspect the existing C++ project and add the calculator with exact decimal arithmetic and focused tests.

The starter contains only a placeholder, so I’m defining a small public API around a `ShippingMethod` enum and using arbitrary-precision integer rationals so no binary floating-point rounding can leak in.

item.text: The environment does not provide Boost, so I’m replacing that dependency with a self-contained decimal-integer implementation. The calculation still stays exact; because all denominators are powers of ten, the final rounding can be done directly from decimal digits.

item.text:
Implemented the exact checkout calculator in [CheckoutPriceCalculator.cpp](/home/gili/cat/worktrees/v1.0/.cat/temp/changelog-language-captures/cpp-code-codex-base.H4ojvy/codex/mss80bq9-zffc5278s/project/CheckoutPriceCalculator.cpp).

It provides `calculate(...)` with standard/expedited shipping (and a boolean convenience overload), validates inputs/rates, applies shipping and tax in the required order, and produces two-decimal half-even-rounded totals without floating-point arithmetic.

Verified with strict compilation and cases covering standard/expedited totals, rate validation, and half-even ties.
